# ASYNCIO.GATHER — concurrent host calls in ONE interpreter
# Python's asyncio.gather dispatches multiple host function
# calls as futures. The bridge resolves them in parallel,
# not one at a time.
import asyncio

async def fetch_users():
    return fetch_json('https://api.example.com/users')

async def fetch_weather():
    return fetch_json('https://api.example.com/weather')

async def get_timestamp():
    return get_time()

async def main():
    # All 3 host functions dispatched concurrently
    users, weather, ts = await asyncio.gather(
        fetch_users(),
        fetch_weather(),
        get_timestamp(),
    )
    return {
        'user_count': len(users),
        'temp': weather['temp'],
        'time': ts,
        'all_resolved': True
    }

asyncio.run(main())
description: Python asyncio.gather within a single interpreter. Multiple host function calls dispatched as futures and resolved concurrently by the bridge.

# 4. Now it's finished

# 5. Free releases resources
sandbox_free(handle=h)
